chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity) and performed ghusl before urinating, and something came out from him. He said: 'He must repeat the ghusl.' I said: 'And for the woman, if something comes out from her after the ghusl?' He said: 'She does not repeat.' I said: 'So what is the difference between the two?' He said: 'Because what comes out from the woman is merely from the water of the man.'

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: Became junub (in a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl)
key_terms.مَاءِ الرَّجُلِ: The water of the man (referring to seminal fluid)

ai.seo_question: Does a woman need to repeat ghusl if she discharges after bathing for janabah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights a nuanced juristic distinction in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of ghusl for janabah, where men must repeat the ritual bath if any discharge occurs post-washing, whereas women are exempt. The Imam attributes this difference to the ontological nature of the discharge, identifying female post-coital fluid as residual seminal fluid ('water of the man'), thereby preserving the completeness of the initial ghusl. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the specific biological and legal definitions of impurities in ritual purification.
